A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work. Their main text, equations, figures, and complete Appendices A–C are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original density-estimation experiments on eight synthetic datasets, including test likelihoods, learned partitions, and training curves in Figures 1–3.

after.justification: v2 retains the synthetic experiments and adds original results on four UCI tabular datasets in Table 1 and Figure 4.

M1.justification: The VT/HFV constructions, certification algorithms, and soft-gating training procedure are retained. The new selective-layer HFV discussion describes an option within a framework that already accommodates standard sum nodes in Appendix A.4.2; no changed experimental implementation is established.

E1.justification: Section 4.2 adds power (6D), gas (8D), hepmass (21D), and miniboone (43D), substantially extending evaluation from synthetic 2D/3D geometry to real tabular density estimation. All eight synthetic datasets remain.

E2.justification: Both versions compare EinsumNet and HCLT with their VT and HFV variants. The added UCI experiments use these same comparator families; newly cited methods are not added as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: The added UCI experiments specify 40 input and sum units, while the retained synthetic experiments use 5 or 10. Section 4.2 states that the training protocol is otherwise identical and reports unrefined VT bounds. Existing experimental settings are unchanged.

E4.justification: New Figure 4 extends training-dynamics and certification-gap diagnostics from the synthetic spiral example to four higher-dimensional tabular datasets. This adds diagnostic evidence without introducing component ablations or controlled robustness tests.

E5.justification: Both versions report means over three trials, without adding run variability, confidence intervals, or significance testing. The additional certified likelihood bounds quantify inference approximation, not statistical uncertainty.

E6.justification: Table 1 and Figure 4 add substantial tabular results; the existing synthetic results are unchanged. For example, the new VT-HCLT lower bound is 5.10 versus HCLT's 0.55 on power, but -26.46 versus -25.43 on miniboone. These are newly reported comparisons, not improvements over corresponding v1 experiments.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, results, algorithms, and Appendix A proofs are substantively unchanged. Adding 'roughly' to Theorem 3.9 reflects the informal rate qualification already present in v1's appendix. The added rotated-hyperplane illustration explains an existing geometric limitation.

C1.justification: The conclusion expands empirical validation from low-dimensional geometric manifolds to synthetic manifolds and tabular benchmarks. The central claims about geometric routing, certified approximation, HFV tractability, and soft-gating convergence remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Section 3.2 expands applicability guidance, including selective HFV gating to avoid full determinism. Section 4.2 interprets widening certification gaps on higher-dimensional datasets through the conservative box construction and existing dimension-dependent analysis.

D1.justification: v2 documents the added tabular models' 40-unit configuration and reuse of the training and unrefined certification procedures. Appendix C's software, hardware, optimizer, annealing, and checkpoint-selection details are unchanged. Tabular preprocessing and data splits are not specified.

R1.justification: v2 adds references including Ventola et al. (2023), Zhao et al. (2016), Liu et al. (2026), and Papamakarios et al. (2017). It also clarifies distinctions from context-conditioned and other input-dependent circuits, while retaining the existing research positioning.

P1.justification: v2 divides experiments into synthetic and tabular subsections, adds an Impact Statement and publication information, and makes localized explanatory and language edits. The overall organization and most prose remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds Table 1 and the four-panel Figure 4. Existing Figures 1–3 are retained and regrouped on page 8; the appendix dataset illustration becomes Figure 5. These are localized display additions and reflow within the existing visual format.

improvement.justification: Section 4.2, Table 1, and Figure 4 strengthen empirical support beyond v1's synthetic 2D/3D demonstrations and make higher-dimensional certification gaps visible. The gain is limited: the bounds remain wide on higher-dimensional datasets, efficient tight certification is not demonstrated, and tabular preprocessing, splits, and run variability remain unspecified.
